role_in_parent: This is the substantive derivative estimate that drives the integral argument.
statement_nl: For every positive integer n, every integer j with 0 ≤ j ≤ n - 1, and every real x with 0 ≤ x < 1/n, the derivative of the function x ↦ K_{n,j}(x) is ≤ 0.

domain_restrictions: j is an integer satisfying 0 ≤ j ≤ n - 1
x is a real number satisfying 0 ≤ x < 1/n
the derivative of K_{n,j} with respect to x exists at the given x and is a real number (existence/definedness is implicit)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all positive integers n, for all integers j with 0 ≤ j ≤ n - 1, and for all real x with 0 ≤ x < 1/n, the derivative with respect to x of the function K_{n,j}(x) exists and is less than or equal to 0.

variables.name: n
variables.role: outer quantifier parameter indexing the family of functions K_{n,j}

variables.name: j
variables.role: index for a specific function K_{n,j} with the constraint 0 ≤ j ≤ n - 1

variables.name: x
variables.role: input point where the derivative of K_{n,j} is evaluated

variables.domain: domain not explicitly specified in the statement; derivative is asserted on 0 ≤ x < 1/n
variables.name: K_{n,j}
variables.role: function whose derivative with respect to x is required to be nonpositive on the stated range
variables.type: real-valued function of a real variable

witness_dependencies: no existential quantifiers; there are no witnesses to choose
the bound on j depends on n
the bound on x depends on n via 1/n
